page.text:
Propositional logic treats complete statements as indivisible units.
Mathematics also needs *open* expressions such as $x^2 < 2$, whose truth
depends on a value assigned to $x$. Predicate logic supplies the missing
structure: variables range over a specified domain, predicates become
statements after their arguments are supplied, and quantifiers assert
that a predicate holds universally or has a witness.
